name: Bermuda
summary_text: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory. The Equality Act 2010 of the United Kingdom and its 2025 single-sex services code do not automatically extend to Bermuda. Local legislation governs, and United Kingdom measures could be applied to Bermuda only by Order in Council.  There is no legal recognition of transgender people in Bermuda. By omission, there is no protection from discrimination for transgender people. The ability of persons to express gender identity is described as often difficult.  The Human Rights Act 1981, as amended by Parliament in 2013, prohibits discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation. That prohibition does not extend to gender identity. A trans visitor therefore has no explicit statutory protection under that Act.  Prior to 1994 anal sex and oral sex were illegal and punishable by up to ten years imprisonment, while lesbian activity was never illegal. On 14 May 1994 the House of Assembly voted 22 to 16 to decriminalise consensual sex between adult men, removing two sections of the Criminal Code through the 1994 Stubbs Bill. That reform legalised consensual sexual conduct in private but retained an unequal age of consent of 18 for gay male conduct versus 16 for heterosexual and lesbian conduct, described as in clear violation of the European Convention on Human Rights.  On 1 November 2019 an amendment to the Criminal Code set 18 years for consensual anal intercourse. As of 2022 the age remains unequal at 18 for anal intercourse versus 16 for other sexual activity. The provision on gross indecency between men was repealed in 2019.  Same-sex marriage was first made legal by Supreme Court ruling in May 2017 finding the Marriage Act 1944 inconsistent with the Human Rights Act. It was then replaced by domestic partnerships under a law passed in December 2017, given royal assent on 7 February 2018 and effective 1 June 2018. The Supreme Court restored same-sex marriage on 6 June 2018 and the Court of Appeal upheld that restoration on 23 November 2018. On 14 March 2022 the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council banned same-sex marriage again, with laws in July 2022 retrospectively backdating legality for the period prior to March 2022. Marriage has not been legally available to same-sex couples since 2022. The Domestic Partnership Act 2017, assented to by the Governor of Bermuda in February 2018, replaced same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships for both same-sex and heterosexual couples, the reversal that made Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality. Same-sex marriage was not permitted in July 2013.  In 2006 the Government attempted to ban Mark Anderson, also known as the drag queen Queen of Bermuda Sybil, from participating in a parade, stating that he contradicted local mores and sensitivities.
